scenes.visual: Portrait pushes in slowly; names and dates appear.

scenes.tts: Leonor Michaelis ran routine tests for a Berlin city hospital by day and, by night, in "a laboratory of the most primitive kind," measured how light twists as sugar breaks apart — a Jewish scientist who held the title of professor but not the salary, chair, or funding, for whom precision became a kind of shelter.
scenes.visual: Day/night rows, polarimeter dial twisting, professor-without-salary/chair/funding chips.
scenes.narration: Leonor Michaelis ran routine tests for a Berlin city hospital by day and, by night, in "a laboratory of the most primitive kind," measured how light twists as sugar breaks apart — a Jewish scientist who held the title of professor but not the salary, chair, or funding, for whom precision became a kind of shelter.

scenes.tts: With Maud Menten — a Canadian who had already earned an M.D. and would earn a Ph.D. when most universities still refused women advanced degrees — he saw why earlier enzyme experiments failed: they looked too late, after byproducts had tangled the reaction.
scenes.visual: Menten credentials; progress curve with the too-late region.
scenes.narration: With Maud Menten — a Canadian who had already earned an M.D. and would earn a Ph.D. when most universities still refused women advanced degrees — he saw why earlier enzyme experiments failed: they looked too late, after byproducts had tangled the reaction.

scenes.tts: So they started at the beginning, buffering the pH and measuring only the initial velocity. Menten's move was to chemically freeze the reaction at precise instants, stopping the slow optical drift that had masked the true rate.
scenes.visual: Start of the curve, buffered pH, initial slope, frozen instants, drifting dial stops.

scenes.tts: Their 1913 equation turned enzymology from a descriptive science into a quantitative one — and they worked together for a single year.
scenes.visual: 1913 equation + hyperbola; descriptive to quantitative; a single year.
scenes.narration: Their 1913 equation turned enzymology from a descriptive science into a quantitative one — and they worked together for a single year.

scenes.tts: Menten went on to develop azo-dye stains still used in pathology today, climbed in the Canadian wilderness, drove a Model T through Pittsburgh in Paris hats, and was passed over for advancement her whole career.
scenes.visual: Four rows: stains, wilderness, Model T and hats, passed over.
